headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: next-ai-draw-io can ingest untrusted documents via MCP/browser while Khoj indexes personal notes and broad egress can amplify misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can process PDFs/text/images and use MCP/browser, so attacker-controlled document content can reach its instruction-following path. Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports broad network egress, making a shared-file or copied-output bridge plausible. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the file-based pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same folder or document set, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests externally authored PDFs or diagrams, malicious instructions can enter its context.
mitigations: Separate input folders per agent.
Disable MCP for next-ai-draw-io unless needed.
Review imported documents before either agent processes them.
Use read-only copies for Khoj indexing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between document ingestion and instruction parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text files, images, and diagrams and can call external model APIs. If they share a workspace or the same files are routed through both, sensitive content can flow into a third-party backend. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF the same notes or PDFs are opened by both agents, sensitive content can be duplicated across systems.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use hosted model APIs, file contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep personal notes out of next-ai-draw-io inputs.
Use local-only models where possible.
Restrict both agents to separate workspaces.
Redact secrets before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem and does not modify git state, while next-ai-draw-io also lacks filesystem-write and git capabilities in the profile. That removes the main shared-write conflict path. The only overlap is broad network egress and API use, which is not enough for a stronger conflict finding.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional filesystem-write tooling, the profile no longer bounds the conflict surface.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared mutable workspaces.
Do not grant extra write tools.
Serialize any external updates through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io is built for AI-assisted visualization and natural-language commands, so it may act on Khoj-produced summaries or extracted facts. Khoj is a retrieval agent over personal notes and documents, which can generate plausible but unverified outputs. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so downstream misrendering or mistaken actions are plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Khoj outputs are pasted into next-ai-draw-io without verification, errors can cascade into diagrams.
IF next-ai-draw-io treats retrieved text as authoritative, it may render or propagate false claims.
mitigations: Require human review before diagram generation.
Cross-check Khoj outputs against source documents.
Use explicit citation fields in prompts.
Mark unverified text as draft.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text files, images, and diagrams and may send them to external model providers. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same document classes.
conditions: IF personal or regulated documents are processed by both agents, retention and residency obligations must be checked.
IF next-ai-draw-io uses hosted APIs for regulated files, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Classify documents before use.
Keep regulated data out of hosted APIs.
Review retention settings in both tools.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
